hook: At 249 employees Docker Desktop costs your company $0; at employee 250, a 200-developer team owes 200 × $15 = $3,000 a month for the same binary. Docker's free tier is a headcount test, not a usage tier, and Podman has no seat to count.

sections.title: Docker licenses the desktop; Podman has no licence to enforce
sections.content:
For teams paying for Docker Desktop, or about to. Prices and terms come from both vendors' own pages, checked November 2026; nothing is benchmarked.

> **Docker:** the engine is open source; the desktop is a licensed product.
> **Podman:** the runtime has no daemon; the desktop has no licence.

Each philosophy forbids something.

- **Docker forbids** free commercial Desktop use past a size line. Docker Engine and Moby stay open source; the desktop binary sits under the Docker Subscription Service Agreement, so SSO, SCIM and hardened builds live behind it.
- **Podman forbids** a sales motion. Podman 6.1.4 and Podman Desktop 1.30.5 are Apache 2.0 with no paid tier: nothing to sell you when you grow.

So the question is not daemon vs daemonless; it is which organisation may legally run the free thing.

sections.title: The bill arrives at employee 250, not at build 10,000
sections.content:
Docker Desktop is free while a company has **fewer than 250 employees AND less than $10 million** in annual revenue. Both must hold. Government entities pay at any size.

| Company | Docker Desktop bill |
|---|---|
| 249 employees, under $10M | $0 |
| 250 employees, or $10M+ revenue | 200 devs × $15 = $3,000/month = $36,000/year |

The software did not change between those rows.

| Plan | Per user/month | Adds |
|---|---|---|
| Personal | $0 | — |
| Pro | $9 | commercial Desktop use, Build Cloud, unlimited private repos |
| Team | $15 | audit logs, role-based access control |
| Business | "Contact us" | SSO, SCIM, Hardened Docker Desktop, Image Access Management |

Read it as a penalty table. Seat pricing punishes hiring, not usage: one container a week costs the same $15 as a thousand.

sections.title: Docker's money buys meters, and each meter is its own decision
sections.content:
Past the seat, paid plans attach meters, at Docker's prices:

| Item | Price | Decision it forces |
|---|---|---|
| Build Cloud | base minutes per plan | Do builds fit the allocation? |
| Testcontainers Cloud | $3/100 min prepaid, $4/100 on demand | Steady enough to prepay? |
| Hardened Images | free for developers; "starting at $5k/repo" in production | How many repos ship? |
| Docker Offload | licences on Team and Business | Worth the sales call it requires? |

At 4,000 Testcontainers minutes a month: 4,000 ÷ 100 = 40 blocks, so 40 × $4 = $160 on demand or 40 × $3 = $120 prepaid. Hardened Images at 12 production repos: 12 × $5,000 = $60,000/year, and "starting at" makes that a floor.

Build Cloud punishes bursty CI: base minutes reset each cycle without accumulating, and bought extras expire.

sections.title: Podman's real bill is the port, and the port ends at a socket
sections.content:
Podman's licence bill is $0. The work is pointing Docker tooling at `podman system service`: a **Docker v1.40** compatibility layer beside the native Libpod API. Socket-activated by systemd, it exits after 5 idle seconds by default.

```bash
# Breaks first: unavailable when Podman runs directly on macOS or Windows
# --time 0: no idle exit, so long CI jobs keep the socket
podman system service --time 0 &
sleep 1  # let the listener bind first
export DOCKER_HOST=unix://$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/podman/podman.sock
# Breaks next: anything needing Docker API newer than v1.40
docker compose up -d
```

That variable is the whole migration for CLI and Compose tooling; handlers using Docker-only API get rewritten. The man page warns:

> "the API grants full access to all Podman functionality, and thus allows arbitrary code execution as the user running the API, with no ability to limit or audit this access"

Rootless narrows whose account is exposed; it does not make the socket safe to share.

sections.title: Vendor-neutral also means nobody sells you control
sections.content:
Podman Desktop is free, Apache 2.0 and, in its own words, "trusted as part of the CNCF". It runs on Linux, macOS and Windows. Red Hat sells enterprise support as a build, the Red Hat Build of Podman Desktop, not as a licence tier.

What the free desktop does not give you:

- SCIM provisioning when someone joins or leaves
- an image access policy like Docker's Image Access Management
- a SOC 2 report from a vendor you hold a contract with
- anyone to call, unless you buy Red Hat's build

Docker Business exists to sell that list. Ask who enforces which registries developers may pull from, and Podman's answer is **you do**.

sections.title: Who should pay Docker, and who should fund the port?
sections.content:
**A company already past the threshold that wants central control and CI minutes should pay Docker.** Business gates SSO, SCIM and Image Access Management; every plan carries Build Cloud minutes.

A small team under the threshold should pick Podman while the port is cheap. So should a large org that wants per-seat × headcount off the budget and can staff the port.

Skip Docker if you are a government entity counting on the free tier; it never applied. Skip Podman if your toolchain needs Docker API above v1.40, or nobody owns socket permissions.

Check today:

1. Headcount and revenue against 250 and $10M. Both limits, not either.
2. Which CI jobs call the Docker API, and at what version.
3. Who can open the socket on your build hosts.

decision_matrix.situation: Under 250 employees and under $10M revenue, nobody asking for SSO
decision_matrix.why: Both cost $0 today, and the port is cheapest before 200 developers depend on Desktop.
Employee 250 bills every commercial Desktop seat at once, so the port or the budget line has to exist before the hire, not after.

decision_matrix.pick: Docker Team, or fund the port
decision_matrix.why: The free tier needs both limits to hold, and the revenue test has already failed.

decision_matrix.pick: Podman, unless you need Business controls
decision_matrix.why: Docker Desktop's free tier never covers government, while Podman has no seat to license.

decision_matrix.situation: 1,000+ engineers, identity team requires SSO, SCIM and registry policy
decision_matrix.why: SSO, SCIM and Image Access Management are gated at Business and Podman Desktop has no equivalent.

decision_matrix.situation: Large org whose platform team owns CI sockets and wants the seat line deleted
decision_matrix.why: Per-seat × headcount goes to $0 and the team can absorb the Docker v1.40 gap and the socket decision.

decision_matrix.situation: Testcontainers-heavy suite, no one to run container sockets on CI hosts
decision_matrix.why: Paying $3–$4 per 100 minutes is cheaper than an unowned socket that grants arbitrary code execution.

decision_matrix.situation: Mid-term on an annual Docker plan with every seat assigned
decision_matrix.why: Only unused seats can be removed and a cancelled plan refunds nothing, so plan the port against the renewal date.

cost_math.label: 25 developers: Team vs Pro
cost_math.result: $4,500/year vs $2,700/year; Pro drops org audit logs and RBAC

verdict_summary: A company already past 250 employees or $10M revenue that wants SSO, SCIM, image policy and CI minutes from one vendor should pay for Docker. A small team under the threshold, or a large org that wants per-seat × headcount off the budget and can fund the port to a Docker v1.40 socket, should run Podman. Count headcount and revenue against both limits before your next Docker renewal.

faqs.q: Can we cut Docker seats mid-contract?
faqs.a: Only unused seats can be removed on Team and Business, and cancelling has no pause and refunds no unused portion; access runs to the end of the paid cycle. An unpaid invoice starts a 15-day grace period.

faqs.q: Is Docker Desktop free for our open-source work?
faqs.a: It is free for non-commercial open source, education and personal use. Commercial use beyond the small-business tier needs a Pro, Team or Business subscription, open source or not.

faqs.q: Can CI reach the Podman API over TCP?
faqs.a: The man page recommends against exposing the socket over TCP without mutual TLS and suggests SSH forwarding instead. The service supports only one listening socket, and the rootful default is unix:///run/podman/podman.sock.

faqs.q: Does Podman Desktop work on a locked-down network?
faqs.a: Podman Desktop lists VPN/proxy support and air-gapped installation options, plus multi-arch builds and GPU acceleration. Those are vendor descriptions, not tested here.
